<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec>
                <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Pakistan is facing a growing population of people living with human immunodeficiency (HIV). In this randomized controlled trial, we investigate if a pharmacist-led intervention can increase adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) for people living with HIV (PLWH).</jats:p>
              </jats:sec><jats:sec>
                <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Adults with HIV, who have been taking ART for more than 3 months were randomly assigned to receive either a pharmacist-led intervention or their usual care. Measures of adherence were collected at 1) baseline 2) just prior to delivery of intervention and 3) 8 weeks later. The primary outcomes were CD4 cell count and self-reported adherence measured with the AIDS Clinical Trial Group (ACTG) questionnaire.</jats:p>
              </jats:sec><jats:sec>
                <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Post-intervention, the intervention group showed a statistically significant increase in CD4 cell counts as compared to the usual care group (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> = 0.0054). In addition, adherence improved in the intervention group, with participants being 5.96 times more likely to report having not missed their medication for longer periods of time (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> = 0.0086) while participants in the intervention group were 7.74 times more likely to report missing their ART less frequently (<jats:italic>p</jats:italic> < 0.0001).</jats:p>
              </jats:sec><jats:sec>
                <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                <jats:p>The findings support the improvement in ART adherence and HIV management.</jats:p>
              </jats:sec><jats:sec>
                <jats:title>Trial registration</jats:title>
                <jats:p>The trial is registered with Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (<jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" ext-link-type="uri" xlink:href="https://www.anzctr.org.au/TrialSearch.aspx#&&conditionCode=&dateOfRegistrationFrom=&interventionDescription=&interventionCodeOperator=OR&primarySponsorType=&gender=&distance=&postcode=&pageSize=20&ageGroup=&recruitmentCountryOperator=OR&recruitmentRegion=&ethicsReview=&countryOfRecruitment=&regist">ACTRN12618001882213</jats:ext-link>). Registered 20 November 2018.</jats:p>
              </jats:sec>
title: Pharmacist-led counselling intervention to improve antiretroviral drug adherence in Pakistan: a randomized controlled trial
